title: The subscription is created before card validation, leaving an orphan incomplete subscription on every typo
description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:210 creates the Stripe subscription before calling elements.submit(). The other three billing components validate first and carry a comment explaining why.
impact: Every mistyped card leaves an orphan incomplete subscription on the customer record, polluting billing data and potentially triggering dunning.
recommendation: Call elements.submit() first, matching components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx.

title: The checkout success page only understands subscriptions, so credit top-ups warn about a payment that succeeded
description: app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:13 is the return_url for all four checkout flows but only polls verify-subscription. A redirect-method credit top-up polls for about 22.5 seconds and then warns the payment could not be confirmed. redirect_status=failed is ignored entirely, so a genuinely failed payment also lands on a page implying success is pending.
impact: A successful purchase is reported as possibly failed, and a failed purchase is reported as probably fine. Both directions are wrong on the money path.
recommendation: Branch on the product type in the return URL and read redirect_status.

title: The support tickets section renders nothing while loading, so /contact looks like the feature is missing
description: components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:174 is `if (isLoading) return null`, under the first and most prominent category on /contact.
impact: On a cold load the page appears not to have a ticket feature at all.
recommendation: Render a skeleton instead of null.

title: /donate removes its own fallback link at the moment it is needed and traps the back button in a redirect loop
description: app/donate/page.tsx:14-22 redirects via window.location.href after 100ms and sets redirected true. At :51-60 the manual 'Continue to Stripe' button renders only when !redirected, and a thank-you message replaces it when redirected. Three defects compound: the fallback disappears exactly when the automatic redirect has failed; location.href rather than location.replace() leaves /donate in history, so Back from Stripe returns here and re-fires after 100ms; and the page has no nav, no <main> and no footer, so a stranded user has no way off it.
impact: A user whose redirect fails is shown a thank-you for a donation that never happened, with no link to complete it and no navigation. Pressing Back from Stripe creates an inescapable loop.
recommendation: Use location.replace(), keep the fallback link rendered unconditionally, drop the premature thank-you, and wrap the page in PublicPageShell.

title: Checkout columns are misaligned between 768px and 1024px by a hardcoded top padding
description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:306 uses a magic md:pt-[120px] to align the second column.
impact: The two columns visibly misalign across the whole tablet band on the payment page.
recommendation: Align with a grid row rather than a hardcoded pixel offset.

title: /checks ships roughly 754 list items and 190KB of HTML that never paints
description: app/checks/page.tsx:147-188 renders an <li> for every one of roughly 754 checks across 18 categories, each with a SeverityPill carrying three inline style properties and a Link, all inside collapsed <details> elements.
impact: Slow first paint on a phone, on the page whose entire purpose is to rank in search and be read by mobile arrivals.
recommendation: Inline only the first N categories and link the rest to the existing /checks/category/[category] pages, or move the full index behind a crawlable ?all=1. The 754 individual check pages are intentional SEO surface and stay.

title: Route error and loading boundaries exist for five routes and are missing on the other eight core routes plus all public content
description: error.tsx exists for /dashboard, /history, /shares, /assets, /teams, /admin, /profile, /compare only. Missing on /repos, /badge, /public-scans, /attack-surface, /host/[hostname], /shared/[token], /browser/[id], /demo, /changelog, /checks, /alternatives, /tools, /docs, /legal, /contact, /pricing, /donate, /security and all of /checkout. loading.tsx has the same gaps, and /checkout has none despite components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx existing. app/dashboard/error.tsx:9-16 states the intent: it keeps the surrounding chrome intact. Additionally app/admin/error.tsx lacks the role="alert" and icon aria-hidden that app/profile/error.tsx:20,26 has.
impact: A thrown error on any of those routes falls through to the root boundary, losing the page chrome and dropping the user onto a bare error screen. That covers roughly 790 public pages, since only /compare has its own boundary.
recommendation: Add error.tsx to the eight missing core routes and to the public content sections, following app/dashboard/error.tsx. Add loading.tsx to /checkout wrapping the existing CheckoutSkeleton. Bring app/admin/error.tsx in line with app/profile/error.tsx.

title: The root 404 has no public chrome and its primary button sends logged-out visitors to the dashboard
description: No in-scope content route has its own not-found.tsx, so all three dynamic content routes fall through to the root one, which renders no LandingNav, no Footer, and a primary button linking to ROUTES.DASHBOARD. The same shape applies to app/error.tsx:103.
impact: A logged-out visitor landing on a stale /checks/some-renamed-id from a search result gets a chrome-less 404 whose main button bounces them through middleware to /login. The likeliest visitor to a dead check URL is exactly the person with no account.
recommendation: Add app/checks/not-found.tsx and app/alternatives/not-found.tsx wrapping SeoPageShell, or make the root 404's primary button conditional on auth and default it to ROUTES.LANDING.

title: The public scans table uses fixed pixel columns that crush the hostname at tablet widths
description: components/public-scans/public-scans-table.tsx:7 and components/public-scans/public-scan-row.tsx:22 use grid-cols-[1fr_150px_150px_90px] with gap-4, which is 390px of fixed columns plus 48px of gaps. At the sm breakpoint (640px) the Site column collapses to about 120px so nearly every hostname truncates, while 'Verdict' renders the word 'Clean' inside 150px.
impact: The one column carrying the information is starved while two columns hold whitespace, on a public directory page.
recommendation: Use sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_90px_150px_120px], or move the grid to the md breakpoint and keep the stacked layout through tablet.

title: The status poll uses a fixed 2000ms sleep with no early wake, adding up to 2 seconds of dead time after the scan completes
description: The client polls GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] on a fixed interval from lib/config/config-values.ts:555, with no backoff and no jitter, first poll immediate (app/dashboard/page.tsx:142, sleep at :160). Nothing wakes the loop when the server finishes.
impact: Adds 0 to 2 seconds, averaging about 1, after the server is already done. Minor next to scan-01 but it becomes a third of the remaining wait once that is fixed.
recommendation: Shorten the interval for the first ~10 seconds, or add SSE / long-poll to the status route.

title: A blurred full-screen AI modal opens the instant results land, so a finished scan reads as still working
description: app/dashboard/page.tsx:690-692 opens AiChoiceModal on completion, a fixed inset-0 backdrop-blur-xs overlay (components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:36). Results render underneath but the user must click Skip to see them.
impact: Perceived latency on top of real latency. The scan finishes and the user is shown a blur, which is indistinguishable from more waiting.
recommendation: Do not auto-open on completion. Offer the AI summary as an action on the results view instead, so the payoff of the scan is the first thing visible.

title: Five different page shells across the public surface, with /pricing hand-rolled and /donate having none
description: PublicPageShell (components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:32) swaps `isLoggedIn ? <Header/> : <LandingNav/>` at :58, covering /changelog, /compare, /contact, /security, /host/[hostname], /public-scans, /shared/[token]. DocsShell, LegalShell and SeoPageShell all use LandingNav unconditionally. /pricing is hand-rolled and renders <LandingNav /> twice (app/pricing/page.tsx:71 and :150) despite computing isLoggedIn at :66. /donate has no nav, no <main> and no footer at all. LandingNav is itself auth-aware (components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:104), so the swap is redundant.
impact: A signed-in user clicking Changelog, then Docs, then Changelog watches the header change identity twice. /donate is a page with no way off it.
recommendation: Move /pricing and /donate onto PublicPageShell and pick one convention for the signed-in header across the four public shells. The non-negotiable half is shell-01: the skip-link id should live in one shell rather than being forgotten by three.

title: Any non-OK teams response logs a signed-in user out
description: app/teams/page.tsx:109-113 is `if (!res.ok) { router.push("/login"); return; }` with no status check. Every sibling gates on 401 and 403 specifically (app/history/page.tsx:226, app/assets/page.tsx:74). The same shape exists at app/profile/page.tsx:296.
impact: A transient 500, 503 or 429 bounces a still-authenticated user to the login screen, which reads as a session bug and erodes trust in the auth system.
recommendation: Gate the redirect on 401 and 403 and render an error state otherwise, matching the sibling pages.

title: Two more product-surface tablists declare tab roles with no tabpanel, aria-controls or arrow-key navigation
description: Extends AUDIT-011#docs-11, which covered components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:30 and app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:420. The same incomplete pattern exists twice more, outside docs: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896-916 renders `role="tablist" aria-label="Code examples"` with `role="tab" aria-selected` buttons over a `<CodeBlock>` at :921 that is not `role="tabpanel"` and carries no id, and no button has `aria-controls`; app/assets/page.tsx:159-183 renders the My-scans / All-public-hosts scope toggle as `role="tablist"` + `role="tab" aria-selected` where the thing it switches is the page's own list, with no tabpanel, no aria-controls and no roving tabindex. Neither has an onKeyDown for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, so the arrow-key roving focus the tab role promises is absent in both. Of the five tablists in the repo, only app/docs/api/page.tsx:1235-1263 is complete (aria-controls="code-tabpanel" at :1246 with a matching role="tabpanel" at :1263).
impact: Assistive tech announces "tab, 1 of 3" and then arrow keys do nothing, which is worse than announcing plain buttons because the user is told a navigation model that is not implemented. On issue-detail this is the fix-example switcher inside every finding, so it is on the product's main output path rather than in docs.
recommendation: For app/assets/page.tsx:159, drop the tablist/tab roles entirely and use `aria-pressed` toggle buttons, which is what the control actually is (the codebase already uses that shape 27 times). For components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896, either do the same or complete the pattern: give CodeBlock a wrapper with `role="tabpanel" id` and `aria-labelledby`, give each button an id and `aria-controls`, and add ArrowLeft/ArrowRight roving focus.

title: The signed-in app header marks the current page with colour alone, with no aria-current, while the landing nav next to it does it correctly
description: components/scanner/header.tsx:153-183 is the primary navigation for every signed-in page. It computes `const active = isNavActive(href)` at :155 and expresses it only as `bg-primary/10 text-primary font-medium` at :166, with no `aria-current`. The `<nav>` at :153 also has no `aria-label`, and neither does the mobile one at :234, so a screen reader lists two or three unnamed navigation landmarks per page. Thirteen other places in the codebase do set aria-current, including the landing nav that renders in exactly the same slot for signed-out users (components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:82 and :159), the docs sidebar (components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx:53), the legal nav (components/legal/legal-nav.tsx:43) and the pagination control (components/ui/pagination-control.tsx:171). The admin link at header.tsx:171-181 has the same gap.
impact: A screen-reader user in the signed-in app is never told which nav item corresponds to the page they are on, and the visual cue that would tell a sighted user is a colour that itself fails contrast in light mode (see a11y-02: text-primary on bg-primary/10 computes to 2.08:1). WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color plus a missed 4.1.2 name-role-value.
recommendation: Add `aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}` to the Link at components/scanner/header.tsx:158 and to the admin Link at :171, matching components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:82. Add `aria-label="Main"` to the nav at :153 and `aria-label="Mobile"` to the one at :234.

title: The risk-score trend chart has no keyboard access and no text alternative for its data series
description: components/host/danger-score-trend.tsx:118-159 renders a recharts AreaChart of up to 30 risk scores for a host. The `<AreaChart>` at :123 does not pass recharts' `accessibilityLayer` prop, so the SVG is not focusable and has no keyboard-driven point navigation; the only way to read a value is `<ChartTooltip>` at :148, which recharts fires on mouse move. There is no `<table>` fallback, no `aria-label` summarising the series, and no `role="img"` with a description. The surrounding text (:91-113) gives only the point count and the delta from oldest to newest, not the series. The product's own accessibility statement pre-declares this at app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:125-128 ("Complex data visualizations: Some security scan result charts may require additional screen reader descriptions"), which is why this is low rather than medium. Worth contrasting with components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:135-142, where the SeverityDistribution bar does the right thing: `role="img"` plus an aria-label that spells out every count.
impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user on a /host/[hostname] page cannot read any individual score in the trend, only that the chart exists. The gap is disclosed rather than hidden, so it is honest, but it is still a WCAG 1.1.1 failure on the page's headline visual.
recommendation: Add `accessibilityLayer` to the AreaChart at components/host/danger-score-trend.tsx:123 (recharts then makes the chart focusable and moves a keyboard cursor through points with arrow keys), and add an sr-only `<table>` or an aria-label built from `toChartData(points)` listing each date and score, mirroring the aria-label approach in components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:137.

title: The competitor comparison table has no scope on its header cells and no caption
description: app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:110-130 renders a three-column comparison table whose `<th>` elements at :113, :116, :119 (column headers) and :127 (a row header per feature) carry no `scope` attribute, and the table has no `<caption>`. Every other table in the repo does this correctly: components/docs/docs-table.tsx uses `scope="col"` / `scope="row"` and an sr-only `<caption>` in all four of its variants (:62, :111, :114-136, :184, :239), components/landing/landing-categories.tsx:83 and components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:193 both have sr-only captions. This one page is the outlier, and it is a generated SEO route so the markup repeats once per competitor.
impact: A screen-reader user navigating the comparison grid cell by cell is not told which column or feature row each cell belongs to, so a table whose whole purpose is a per-row VulnRadar-versus-competitor comparison reads as a flat list of Yes/No values. WCAG 1.3.1.
recommendation: Add `scope="col"` to app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:113, :116, :119 and `scope="row"` to :127, plus an sr-only `<caption>` naming the comparison, copying components/docs/docs-table.tsx:111-114.

title: Markdown H1s in AI chat replies inject additional h1 elements into whatever page the widget is open on
description: components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx:24 and the duplicate map in components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:207 render a markdown `#` heading as `<h1 className="text-sm font-semibold mt-3 mb-1.5 first:mt-0" {...props} />`. The ChatWidget is mounted globally from app/layout.tsx:190, so an assistant reply containing a top-level markdown heading emits a second (or third) `<h1>` into the current page's heading tree, at a font size of 14px and nested inside a `role="dialog"`. The model's output is not constrained here, and the docs knowledge files it draws from are markdown with `#` headings.
impact: A screen-reader user navigating by heading level on, say, /dashboard finds extra top-level headings that belong to a chat message rather than the page, and the document outline no longer matches the visual hierarchy. Bounded: it only occurs while the widget is open and only for replies that use a top-level heading.
recommendation:
Demote the mapping in both files: render markdown `#` as `

` (or `

`) inside the chat transcript, and shift h2/h3 down accordingly, so nothing inside the widget competes with the page's own h1.

title: Input and card borders sit at 1.21:1 to 1.54:1 against their own surfaces, below the 3:1 non-text minimum
description: app/globals.css:194-195 sets light `--border`/`--input: 213 16% 78%` against `--background: 213 25% 90%` (:172) and `--card: 213 22% 95%` (:174), and :240-241 sets dark `--border`/`--input: 224 15% 16%` against `--background: 224 20% 6%` (:224) and `--card: 224 18% 9%` (:226). Computed: light border vs background 1.36:1 and vs card 1.54:1; dark border vs background 1.28:1 and vs card 1.21:1. components/ui/input.tsx:11 gives every field `border border-input bg-background` and no other visual boundary, so the border is the sole indicator of where the control is. WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast requires 3:1 for the visual boundary of a UI component when that boundary is what identifies it.
impact: On a card, an unfilled text field is nearly indistinguishable from the surface it sits on for a low-vision user, in both themes. Low because a filled field's own text and the layout still convey where to type, and because the fields are labelled.
recommendation: Split --border from --input in app/globals.css and darken/lighten only --input to clear 3:1 against both --background and --card in each theme (light around `213 16% 55%`, dark around `224 12% 38%`), leaving --border for decorative dividers where 3:1 is not required.

title: Ninety-five lines of hover and selection CSS with thirteen literal HSL colours and !important have zero consumers anywhere in the repo
description: app/globals.css:483-575 defines five utility classes with a documented purpose: .hover-surface ("Use .hover-surface on any interactive element for consistent hover feedback", :485), .hover-surface-subtle, .scanner-selected, .scanner-selected-hover and .scanner-hover. Grepping app/, components/, lib/, scripts/, cli/ and extension/ for any of the five names returns matches only inside globals.css itself. They are dead. design-language.md A3 item 7 already noted that this block hardcodes hover surfaces as literal HSL with !important; what it did not check is that nothing uses them. The block hardcodes thirteen literal colour values that bypass the token system entirely (hsl(220 10% 88% / 0.95), hsl(220 15% 12%), hsl(220 8% 24% / 0.95), hsl(220 10% 92%), hsl(220 10% 85% / 0.5), hsl(220 8% 28% / 0.5), hsl(220 10% 75% / 0.55), hsl(220 8% 30% / 0.55), hsl(220 10% 70% / 0.7), hsl(220 8% 35% / 0.65), hsl(220 10% 50% / 0.12), hsl(220 8% 70% / 0.1), hsl(220 15% 10%)), six of them with !important, and duplicates each one across a .dark twin. The Radix menu-item rules at :519-537 in the same block DO have consumers (every dropdown and select), so the block is not entirely dead and cannot be deleted wholesale.
impact: Ninety-five lines of CSS ship to every visitor for nothing. More usefully, it is a trap: the comment tells the next developer this is the standard way to do a hover state, so a new component adopts it, gets an !important that overrides its own hover:bg-muted/40, and gets a grey that is not a token and will not track a palette change.
recommendation: Delete the .hover-surface, .hover-surface-subtle, .scanner-selected, .scanner-selected-hover and .scanner-hover rules and their .dark twins (app/globals.css:481-517 and :539-575), leaving the [data-radix-menu-content] rules at :519-537 which are live. Rewrite those surviving rules to use tokens instead of literals: background-color: hsl(var(--accent)); color: hsl(var(--accent-foreground)); which is what --accent (213 18% 81% light / 220 8% 22% dark) exists for, and drop the .dark duplicate since the token already switches. Then the documented hover convention becomes `hover:bg-muted/40` or `hover:bg-accent`, which is what the live components already do.

title: components/ui/badge.tsx's four untokenised variants are not merely off-palette, they have zero call sites, so removing them is free
description: Extends AUDIT-011#design-03, which filed components/ui/badge.tsx:16-19 as the one primitive that hardcodes Tailwind palette colours (bg-blue-500/10 text-blue-600, bg-green-500/10 text-green-600, bg-amber-500/10 text-amber-600, bg-red-500/10 text-red-600) and does not respond to dark mode. What was not established is whether anything uses them. It does not. Across app/ and components/ there are 102 <Badge> instances in 32 files; the only variant values passed are "outline" (5) and "secondary" (7), with the rest defaulting. There is no variant="info", variant="success", variant="warning" or variant="error" anywhere, and badgeVariants is not called directly outside badge.tsx:35. The 60-odd `variant="info"` and `variant="warning"` matches in app/docs/ belong to DocsCallout and LegalCallout, a different component (see dsn-12). Separately, 14 of the 102 instances pass a className that overrides the variant's colours entirely, for example app/admin/page.tsx:1442's `bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-500 border-emerald-500/20`, which is the pattern that would have used variant="success" if it worked in dark mode.
impact: The fix AUDIT-011#design-03 asked for looked like it needed a migration and therefore did not happen. It needs no migration. Meanwhile the dead variants sit in the primitive as the apparent house answer for semantic badges, which is why 14 call sites reached past them for a raw palette className instead.
recommendation: Delete lines 16-19 of components/ui/badge.tsx outright; nothing imports them. Then add one tokenised replacement so the 14 className-override sites have somewhere to go: a `tone` prop taking neutral | primary | success | warning | destructive | severity, resolving to `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--success-text))] border-[hsl(var(--success))]/25` and siblings using the foreground tokens from dsn-01. Migrate the raw-palette call sites to it: app/admin/page.tsx:1430,1442,1577, components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:666,915,1039,1051, components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:86, components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:570,689 and components/profile/tabs/developer/schedules-section.tsx:304 (the last of which is also the only dark: override in the whole app outside the landing page).

title: Three lookup tables paint status with raw Tailwind palette colours instead of the tokens beside them, including one that reimplements the severity scale the product has a single source of truth for
description: design-language.md A2 records that the codebase is genuinely clean of raw Tailwind palette colours; the exceptions it names are components/ui/badge.tsx and the globals.css safelist. Three more exist, all in lookup tables where a token equivalent is already in use one line away. (1) components/badge/badge-types.ts:27-36 returns text-red-500 / text-amber-500 / text-emerald-500 and bg-red-500/10 / bg-amber-500/10 / bg-emerald-500/10 from getSeverityColor and getSeverityBg, a second severity scale beside the single source of truth at components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:37-78; consumed by components/badge/badge-scan-list.tsx:91,96,101,130. That is tell-tale 9 (severity via SEVERITY_TONE) failing. (2) components/teams/teams-types.ts:62-70 mixes vocabularies inside one table: owner and admin use tokens (--warning, primary), manager uses indigo-500 and operator uses orange-500, member and viewer use --muted. (3) components/shared/stat-icon.tsx:13-14 and its duplicate at components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:13-14 carry purple-500 and orange-500 among otherwise tokenised tones. Smaller instances: app/admin/page.tsx:1430,1442,1577 and components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:666,915,1039,1051,1997 use amber-500 and emerald-500; components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:412 uses purple-500; components/admin/utils.ts:209 uses emerald-500; components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:309,1349 and components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:114 use emerald-500; app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:288 sets an h1 to text-emerald-500. app/globals.css:9 then safelists eleven of these literal classes with @source inline because the role-badge lookup lives outside Tailwind's content globs.
impact: Since the whole product uses exactly three `dark:` overrides (the theme is entirely token-driven), a raw palette colour is a colour that does not participate in theming at all, and every one of these lands in the light-mode contrast band measured in dsn-01: amber-500 on its own tint is 1.79:1 in light mode, emerald-500 is 2.07:1, orange-500 is 2.27:1. Table (1) also means the /badge page rates a scan on a scale that can drift from the real one, which is precisely what severity-badge.tsx's docblock exists to prevent.
recommendation: (1) Delete getSeverityColor and getSeverityBg from components/badge/badge-types.ts and have components/badge/badge-scan-list.tsx call severityTone() from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx, mapping its safe/caution/unsafe rating onto info/medium/critical. (2) In components/teams/teams-types.ts change manager to `bg-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--chart-4))] border-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]/20` only if a fifth hue is genuinely needed; better, drop the per-role hue entirely and distinguish roles by the existing ROLE_ICONS plus a neutral badge, keeping the accent for owner alone. (3) After dsn-06 merges the two tone tables, replace purple-500 and orange-500 in the surviving components/shared/stat-icon.tsx with `bg-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]` and `--chart-3`, which are the tokens for exactly this job. Then the @source inline safelist at app/globals.css:9 can shrink to whatever the role-badge lookup still needs.

title: The pricing table lifts and shadows its highlighted plan, the only hover-lift-and-shadow treatment in the product
description: components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:72 gives the popular plan `border-primary bg-card shadow-lg shadow-primary/10 lg:-translate-y-1.5` while its three siblings get `border-border/50 bg-card/50`. design-language.md D1 records that shadows in this system are near-invisible (shadow-xs on the shadcn Card, `shadow-xs shadow-black/5` on the hero readout) and tell-tale 10 names `hover:shadow-xl hover:-translate-y-1` as the fail case. This is the static version of it: a coloured glow plus a 6px lift, and it is the only elevated-and-offset card in app/ or components/ outside a modal. The card is already differentiated three other ways (a full-opacity primary border against /50 siblings, a full-opacity bg-card against /50, and an absolutely positioned "Most picked" pill at :77), so the shadow and the lift are the fourth and fifth signals for one fact.
impact: Small, but it is on the page whose entire job is to look trustworthy, and the lift is the single most recognisable marketing-template gesture in web design. Anyone who has seen a SaaS pricing page recognises it immediately, which undercuts the honest-and-specific positioning the landing page spends nine sections building.
recommendation: Change components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:72 to `border-primary bg-card`, dropping shadow-lg, shadow-primary/10 and lg:-translate-y-1.5. The border-versus-border/50 and bg-card-versus-bg-card/50 contrast plus the pill at :77 already carry it, and it matches how the landing page marks its one flagship table row (components/landing/landing-categories.tsx, `border-primary/25 bg-primary/5`, no shadow, no offset). If more emphasis is wanted, add `bg-primary/5` to the popular card rather than elevation.

title: The CSV export writes no UTF-8 BOM, so Excel on Windows mojibakes the same arrows the PDF garbles
description: exportCsv (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:224-252) joins the rows and builds `new Blob([csv], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8;" })` at :250 with no byte order mark. The charset parameter on a Blob MIME type is not written into the file and has no effect on what a spreadsheet application infers when the file is opened from disk. Excel on Windows defaults a .csv with no BOM to the system ANSI code page, so the same 96 non-ASCII characters catalogued in dsnx-01 come back as mojibake: the fixSteps column carries U+2192 in over ten secrets-extended.json entries and is exported at :244 as `f.fixSteps.join(" | ")`, and the description column carries U+00A7 from email.json. The Markdown, SARIF and JSON exports are unaffected because their consumers all assume UTF-8.
impact: CSV is the export a non-engineer picks, and the column it damages is the remediation instructions. A security lead who pulls the findings into a spreadsheet to assign work distributes rows reading "Revoke the token immediately via GitHub Settings â†' Developer Settings".
recommendation: Prefix the BOM at components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:250: `new Blob(["\uFEFF", csv], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8;" })`. Apply the same change to the other CSV writer in the repo, app/api/v3/admin/audit-log/export/route.ts, and to components/compare/compare-actions-menu.tsx if it builds one. Better, move the blob construction into lib/ui/download.ts as `downloadCsv(rows, filename)` next to the existing escapeCsv helper (lib/ui/download.ts:23) so the BOM is applied once and every future CSV inherits it. While there, add the four summary lines the PDF and Markdown reports carry (url, scanned at, safety rating, severity counts) as a commented preamble or a second sheet-style header block, since the CSV is currently the only export with no scan context at all.

title: The compliance crosswalk is the one report with no rendered form: it exports as raw Markdown to the audience least likely to read Markdown
description: exportCompliance (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:276-280) calls generateComplianceReport and downloads the result as `text/markdown` with a `-compliance-<date>.md` filename. lib/reports/compliance-report.ts maps every finding onto PCI DSS 4.0, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and OWASP ASVS controls (via lib/reports/compliance-mappings.ts, 17 KB of mappings) and is genuinely substantial work, but the only output is a plain .md file. app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:37-42 offers the same four formats and compliance is likewise md-only there, while pdf is available for the standard report. The named audience for this report, in the module's own docblock (compliance-report.ts:14-18), is "an engineer or a GRC reviewer", and a GRC reviewer's tooling is documents, not .md files. The menu label is also "Compliance report" (:569) while every sibling entry says "Export as X", so the format is not signalled anywhere before the download lands.
impact: The most enterprise-facing artifact in the product is the only one that arrives in a format its intended reader cannot open in the tool they use. A reviewer handed a .md file either opens it as plain text with the pipe tables unrendered, or asks the engineer to convert it, which is the friction this feature exists to remove.
recommendation: Two steps, in order. First, cheap: change the menu label at components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:569 to "Export compliance crosswalk (Markdown)" so the format is honest before the click, matching the sibling labels. Second, add a PDF path: refactor lib/reports/pdf-report.ts so the layout primitives (addText, addLine, addRect, addTextRight, the page assembly at :435-513) become an exported `PdfBuilder`, then add lib/reports/compliance-pdf.ts that consumes the same ControlBucket structure compliance-report.ts already builds (:100-120) and renders it as a cover page naming the four frameworks and the disclaimer, one section per framework, and one table per control with its findings. Wire it as `format=compliance-pdf` in app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:37 and as a second menu entry. That refactor also pays for itself against dsnx-02, dsnx-09 and dsnx-10, since all three touch the same primitives.

title: Seven in-app logo renders hardcode /favicon.svg or /favicon.png while LOGO_URL exists as both a constant and an admin setting, so a self-hoster's configured logo appears only in email and JSON-LD
description: lib/config/constants.ts:205 defines `LOGO_URL = process.env.LOGO_URL || `${APP_URL}${CONFIG_LOGO_URL}``, .env.example:94-95 documents the LOGO_URL override, and lib/config/registry.ts registers LOGO_URL as a build-tier setting. Only two places consume it: lib/email/email.ts:111-113 (the email header image) and components/seo/structured-data.tsx:92 (Organization logo). Seven other renders hardcode the asset path instead: app/manifest.ts:27 and :28 (PWA install icons), app/layout.tsx:63, :64 and :66 (favicon and apple-touch-icon), components/shared/themed-logo.tsx:27 (the shared logo component used in the header and footer) and components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1345. Separately, components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:56 builds the admin's email preview with a hardcoded `${appUrl}/favicon.svg`, so the preview diverges from the real email whenever LOGO_URL is set.
impact: A self-hoster who sets LOGO_URL to their own mark sees it in outgoing email and in structured data, and nowhere in the product. Every header, footer, browser tab, PWA install icon and AI chat avatar keeps rendering public/favicon.svg. The practical workaround (overwrite public/favicon.svg and public/favicon.png) is fine but undocumented, and it is not available on the pinned-image Docker path where public/ is baked in. The admin email preview showing a different logo than the mail that actually goes out is a small correctness bug on top.
recommendation: Either use the constant where it is a same-origin path (components/shared/themed-logo.tsx:27 and components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1345 can use CONFIG_LOGO_URL, the relative form, rather than the absolute LOGO_URL), or document in app/docs/config/page.tsx's branding section that the in-app logo is the file public/favicon.svg and LOGO_URL only affects email and structured data. Fix components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:56 to use LOGO_URL either way so the preview matches lib/email/email.ts:111-113.

title: The scan-tag input accepts 50 characters and tells the user so, while the server truncates at the admin-configurable MAX_TAG_LENGTH of 30 with no feedback
description: components/history/scan-tags.tsx:15 sets MAX_CLIENT_TAG_LENGTH = 50, used for the maxLength attribute at :165 and for the error copy at :73, `Keep tags under ${MAX_CLIENT_TAG_LENGTH} characters.` The server does not reject an overlong tag: app/api/v3/scan/tags/route.ts:70-:71 reads getSetting('MAX_TAG_LENGTH') and silently truncates with `tag.trim().toLowerCase().slice(0, maxTagLength)`. The default is 30 (lib/config/config-values.ts:1039, admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:2705). The component's own doc comment at :8-:14 acknowledges the split, explaining that 50 is the VARCHAR(50) column guard rather than the enforced limit, so the divergence is deliberate; the message shown to the user is not.
impact: A tag between 31 and 50 characters is accepted by the form, sent, silently shortened, and comes back as a different string than the user typed, with the error copy having just promised them 50 characters were fine. On a deployment that lowered MAX_TAG_LENGTH further, the gap widens with no UI change.
recommendation: Expose MAX_TAG_LENGTH through the existing client config endpoint (app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts already carries FEATURE_PDF_REPORTS), use it for both maxLength and the error copy, and keep 50 only as the hard column guard it is documented to be.

title: The auth SWR cache window is a bare 300000 literal that two other files describe as '5 minutes' in prose
description: components/providers/auth-provider.tsx:90 sets `dedupingInterval: 300000` with no named constant. Three comments elsewhere restate that number in words and build reasoning on it: the same file at :153 ('dedupingInterval (5 minutes)'), app/profile/page.tsx:508-:516 (which explains that without a refreshAuthCache() call a saved setting 'stayed invisible to every other page for up to 5 minutes'), and components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:121-:123 ('a just-canceled plan stays visible elsewhere (paywalls, nav, dashboard) for up to 5 minutes'). A related pair of numbers has the same problem: app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts:36 sends `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` while lib/config/runtime-config.ts:23 holds the server-side settings snapshot for TTL_MS = 30_000, so a flag change takes up to 90 seconds to reach a browser and neither number references the other.
impact: Halving the deduping interval to make saved settings propagate faster leaves three comments across two other files asserting a window that no longer exists, and those comments are the only record of why refreshAuthCache() must be called at each of those save sites.
recommendation: Name it (AUTH_CACHE_DEDUPE_MS in components/providers/auth-provider.tsx, exported) and have the two profile comments reference the constant rather than restating the number. Add a one-line note at app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts:36 tying its max-age to lib/config/runtime-config.ts's TTL_MS so the combined propagation delay is visible in one place.

title: The same five-step checkout retry ladder is copy-pasted into four billing components, giving an unnamed and unadjustable 8-second webhook confirmation budget
description: `const delays = [500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000];` appears verbatim in components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:66, components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx:77, components/billing/browserbase-credit-checkout.tsx:72 and components/billing/github-credit-checkout.tsx:71, each followed by the same `for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= delays.length; attempt++)` loop that polls the confirm endpoint six times and then falls through to a 'pending' state. Total wall-clock budget is 8 seconds. Nothing names the array, nothing explains why five steps, and there is no constant tying the budget to how long the Stripe webhook typically takes to land.
impact: If Stripe's webhook is slower than 8 seconds, all four purchase flows show a pending state to a user who has just been charged, and a maintainer widening the window has to find and edit four identical arrays. A partial edit leaves the credit purchases and the subscription purchase behaving differently for the same underlying delay.
recommendation: Extract the ladder to one exported constant (CHECKOUT_CONFIRM_BACKOFF_MS in a shared billing module) and import it in all four components, with a comment recording the total budget so the next person changing it knows what they are trading against.

title: "Get Started" is the primary CTA label in the nav and on three pricing surfaces, and it is the one string on the marketing surface that says nothing
description: components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:124 labels the logged-out primary nav button "Get Started". The same string appears at app/pricing/page.tsx:93 (the billing-disabled page's only CTA) and components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:170 (the logged-out paid-plan CTA). It is title case where the rest of the page is sentence case, it names no action, and it is the exact label a generated landing page would use. audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F2.4 already records it as the weakest string on the page; this extends that with the two pricing occurrences and with what to put there instead. The full logged-out CTA map above the fold today is: nav "Get Started" to /signup, hero primary "Start scanning free" to /signup, hero secondary "Try the demo" to /demo. Two of three lead to a signup form, and the third leads to a demo that cannot scan the visitor's site (mkt-01). Every other CTA on the page is written properly: "Create a free account", "Try the demo first", "See a full report", "Try it in the playground", "Read the API docs", "Paste a URL and see what comes back".
impact: Minor on its own, but it is the first button a visitor sees and it is inconsistent with a page whose entire argument is specificity. On the billing-disabled self-host page it is also the only CTA, so the whole page ends on the most generic string available.
recommendation: If mkt-01 ships, make the logged-out nav CTA "Scan a URL" pointing at ROUTES.DEMO and leave the ghost "Log in" beside it, so the fastest action is the one in the nav. If it does not, use "Start free" at components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:124. At app/pricing/page.tsx:93 use "Create an account" for the logged-out case, since that page's whole point is that there is nothing to pay for. At components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:170 use "Start free, upgrade later", which is accurate: the button goes to /signup rather than to checkout.

title: The compare run fails silently, leaving the picker on screen with no explanation when a diff is rejected
description: runCompare (app/compare/page.tsx:54-65) sets loading, fetches the compare endpoint with a and b, and does `if (res.ok) setDiffResult(data)` with no else, plus `catch { /* ignore */ }` at :61-63. setLoading(false) then runs at :64 either way. The same function is the deep-link handler at :79, so a stale or invalid ?a=&b= pair in a bookmarked URL takes the same path.
impact: Pressing Compare on two scans the server refuses to diff (different hosts, a scan deleted since the list loaded, a permissions failure) stops the spinner and returns the user to the same picker with both scans still selected and no message, so the only available conclusion is that the button is broken. A shared /compare?a=..&b=.. link whose scans have aged out of retention behaves identically.
recommendation: Add an error state to app/compare/page.tsx, set it from data.error in an !res.ok branch and from the catch, and render it above the Compare button at :275-292 using the same destructive-tinted box the rest of the app uses. For the deep-link path at :78-82, distinguish "these two scans cannot be compared" from "one of these scans no longer exists" and offer handleReset (:200) as the recovery action.

title: Disconnecting an OAuth provider sets a success message and then immediately reloads the page, so the confirmation is dead code the user never sees
description: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:129-131 calls setSuccess with a disconnect confirmation and then window.location.reload() on the next line, so the banner at app/profile/page.tsx:688 is never painted before the document is torn down. The Discord disconnect at :555-558 is identical and additionally discards the server's message on failure at :560 in favour of a generic string, the only place on this tab that does. The user's only feedback for a successful disconnect is a full page refresh.
impact: Disconnecting a sign-in provider is a security-relevant change with no confirmation that it happened. On a slow connection the refresh reads as an unexplained page reset, and a user who is not sure whether it worked will try again.
recommendation: Replace the reload with a targeted state update: the handler already knows which provider was removed, so drop it from the local connections list and call refreshAuthCache() from components/providers/auth-provider, the way components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:101 does after its own mutation. Then the success message survives. If a reload is genuinely required, move the message to the toast from qolf-07 with a sessionStorage handoff read after the reload. Also stop discarding data.error at :560.

title: The teams member list has no search, sort or pagination and the selected team is not addressable by URL, so Back leaves the page entirely
description: app/teams/page.tsx imports nothing from lib/ui/url-state, so no state on the page reaches the URL: selectedTeam (:56), searchQuery (:49), viewingMember (:89) and scanPage (:95) are all useState. Opening a team is openTeam (:296) mutating state in place with no history entry, so browser Back navigates off /teams entirely rather than returning to the team list, and a team cannot be linked or bookmarked. The member list rendered at :588-603 has no search, no role filter, no sort and no pagination, and pending invites are interleaved with members with no way to isolate them.
impact: Sharing "the acme team page" with a colleague is impossible; the only shareable thing is /teams. Back behaving as leave-the-page is the kind of small wrongness users learn to work around by never using Back on that page. The member list is fine at five seats and unusable at fifty, which is the size at which a team feature starts to matter commercially.
recommendation: Back selectedTeam with useQueryParam("team", "") from lib/ui/url-state.ts:170, the same hook app/repos/page.tsx:134 uses for ?repo, resolving the team from the loaded list on mount so a deep link works, and do the same for viewingMember. Add a name and email search plus a role filter above the member list, both URL-backed per qolf-10, and reuse the existing PaginationControl past roughly 20 members. Separately: there is no member role-change mutation in the UI at all, roles are set only at invite time (:70-72), so an owner who invites someone as a viewer must remove and re-invite them to promote them.

title: The /attack-surface page lights no navigation item, so a top-level destination reads as being outside the app
description: isNavActive at components/scanner/header.tsx:88-98 treats /public-scans and /assets as belonging to the History nav item, because both are tabs under components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx. That tab list has four entries (:8-13) and the fourth, ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE, is not in the header's check at :95-97. /attack-surface is also not in NAV_LINKS (:25-34), so navigating there leaves every nav item unlit.
impact: The header stops telling the user where they are on one of the four pages reachable from the history tab strip, which is a small but real "did I leave the app" moment on a page that is otherwise a first-class destination with its own heading and description.
recommendation: Add ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE to the disjunction at components/scanner/header.tsx:95-97 alongside PUBLIC_SCANS and ASSETS. Better, export the TABS array from components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13 and derive the check from it, so the next tab added there cannot desynchronise the header again.

title: The extendedPanels prop on ScanResultDetail and its entire alternate branch are dead, and its doc comment describes a caller that does not exist
description:
`extendedPanels` is declared at components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:53, defaulted to true at :96, and branched on at :150. Its doc comment at :50-56 states that the host-aggregate report sets it false because its data source only carries response headers. A repo-wide grep for extendedPanels across app/ and components/ returns three hits, all inside scan-result-detail.tsx itself. app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:272-288, the host-aggregate report the comment names, does not pass it. So the false branch at :211-218, which renders a response-headers-only version of the More about this host block, has never rendered.

Because the host report takes the true branch, it renders the full panel set. The panels that have no data return null on their own (threat-intel-panel.tsx:36, software-inventory-panel.tsx:35, dns-records-panel.tsx:187, port-scan-panel.tsx:104), which is why nothing looks broken and why the dead branch has gone unnoticed.
impact: A reader of this file is told the host report behaves one way when it behaves another, which is the kind of stale comment that makes the next person reorder the panels wrongly. It is eight lines of unreachable JSX plus a prop that every caller must now reason about.
recommendation: Delete the prop declaration at :53, the default at :96, the ternary at :150 and :211-218, and the doc comment at :50-56, leaving the extended block unconditional. Do this as part of the reorder in qols-08 so the file is touched once. If the response-headers-only variant is still wanted for the host report, make it real by passing `extendedPanels={false}` from app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:272 and keeping the branch; but nothing in the current host API response justifies it, since the panels already self-suppress.

title: A completed scan pushes a history entry, so Back wipes the results and Forward then triggers a full document reload into /history
description:
On completion, `updateUrlWithScan` calls `setQueryParams({ scan: String(id), mode: null, screenshot: null, port_scan: null, active_probes: null })` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:290-296 with no options object. lib/ui/url-state.ts:140-141 defaults to `pushState` when `opts.replace` is falsy, so finishing a scan pushes a new browser history entry.

The consequences chain. Pressing Back returns to the pre-scan URL, which fires `LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT` through the bridge at url-state.ts:29-48, which runs `syncFromUrl` (page.tsx:305-330), which sees no `scan` param with `status === "done"` and clears `result`, `scanHistoryId`, `crawlInfo` and the rest (:309-319). The results are gone. Pressing Forward then returns to `?scan=<publicId>` with `status` now `"idle"`, so the same effect takes the other branch at :326-329 and runs `window.location.href = \`${ROUTES.HISTORY}?scan=...\``, a full document navigation into a different route.

By contrast the same helper is called with `{ replace: true }` for the clearing case at :298, so the intent to replace rather than push is already present in the file, just not on the completion path.
impact: Back after a scan destroys the result the user is looking at, and Forward, the obvious undo, does not restore it: it reloads the whole application into the History page. Minor because the scan is saved and reachable, but it makes the browser's own controls behave unpredictably on the product's main flow.
recommendation: Pass `{ replace: true }` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:290 so a finished scan replaces the launch URL rather than stacking on it. Back then leaves the dashboard entirely, which is what the user means. If the push is deliberate so that Back acts as "clear this result", then the Forward branch must be a soft navigation instead: replace `window.location.href` at :328 with `router.replace(...)` from `next/navigation`, which is worth doing regardless, since a full document load to reach a scan the user was just looking at is the slowest possible path on the page whose whole pitch is speed.

title: Every one of the 805 sitemap URLs carries the same lastmod, the build timestamp, so the field is noise on a 749-page set whose source data changes a few entries at a time
description: app/sitemap.ts:13 computes `const lastModified = new Date()` once and assigns it to every entry at line 17. The comment at lines 10-12 explains the choice as avoiding per-entry timestamp noise, which is right about not calling new Date() per row but produces the opposite of the intended effect: because the route is `force-static` (line 7), the value is frozen at build time and every deploy republishes all 805 URLs with a brand-new identical lastmod. Google's documented position is that it uses lastmod only when it is consistently accurate, and that a site claiming every page changed at the same instant is a signal to ignore the field site-wide. The real modification data exists: the 749 check entries come from lib/scanner/checks-data/*.json (file mtime or git log), the 5 alternatives from lib/seo/alternatives.ts, and the docs pages from their own source files.
impact: The sitemap gives Google no usable freshness signal for 805 URLs, so recrawl scheduling falls back to Google's own heuristics, and the one check page that actually changed after a release is refreshed no sooner than the 748 that did not. On a deploy-frequent repo (3.7.2 with a per-change changelog policy) this republishes the entire sitemap as "all changed" several times a week.
recommendation: Derive lastmod from source. Simplest accurate version: in scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs, which already runs on every prebuild, emit a `{ checkId: isoDate }` map from `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <file>` per checks-data JSON file into lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts, and have CHECK_ROUTES in lib/seo/routes.ts:80 carry a per-route lastModified read from it. Do the same for the docs routes once seo-05 derives them from DOCS_PAGES, using each layout.tsx's git commit date. Keep a single build-time fallback for routes with no source mapping.

title: The PWA manifest is incoherent: start_url is the auth-gated /dashboard, favicon.png is declared 512x512 but is actually 1024x1024, and there is no maskable icon, no id and no screenshots
description: app/manifest.ts:21 sets `start_url: ROUTES.DASHBOARD` ("/dashboard"), a route that requires a session (middleware.ts:332 redirects anonymous requests to /login) and is Disallowed in robots.txt (lib/seo/routes.ts:110). Anyone who installs the PWA while signed out, or after their session expires, launches into a login redirect. Line 28 declares `{ src: "/favicon.png", sizes: "512x512", type: "image/png" }` but the file is 1024x1024 (read from its PNG IHDR, 93.9 KB), so the declared size does not match the asset; Chrome selects icons by the declared value and DevTools reports the mismatch. There is no icon with `purpose: "maskable"`, so Android renders the square PNG letterboxed inside the adaptive-icon mask. There is no `id`, so changing start_url later would be treated as a different app by Chrome. There is no `screenshots` array, so Android shows the minimal install prompt rather than the richer one. Separately, the same 1024x1024 / 94 KB PNG is the apple-touch-icon (app/layout.tsx:66, `apple: "/favicon.png"`) where 180x180 is the used size, so iOS downloads roughly 32 times the pixels it renders.
impact: A user who installs the app gets an icon that looks wrong on Android and a launch that dumps them at a login screen. The apple-touch-icon costs ~94 KB on iOS home-screen add. None of this is visible in search results, but the manifest is part of the installability surface Lighthouse scores and part of what the product looks like when someone takes it seriously enough to install it.
recommendation: In app/manifest.ts: set `start_url: "/"` (middleware.ts:284-288 already routes anonymous to /landing and signed-in to /dashboard, which is exactly the desired behaviour); add `id: "/"`; correct the PNG entry to `sizes: "1024x1024"` or export a real 512x512; add a second entry `{ src: "/icon-maskable.png", sizes: "512x512", type: "image/png", purpose: "maskable" }` with the mark inset to the safe zone; add `screenshots` using the existing 1200x630 card or purpose-shot captures with `form_factor: "wide"` and `"narrow"`. Export a 180x180 apple-touch-icon and point app/layout.tsx:66 at it instead of the 1024px file. The generation can reuse scripts/build-og-image.mjs's sharp pipeline.

title: The homepage URL never serves content: / issues a temporary 307 to /landing for anonymous visitors, and the root layout's fallback canonical points at that same redirecting URL
description: middleware.ts:284-289 redirects an anonymous request for "/" to ROUTES.LANDING with NextResponse.redirect(), which defaults to HTTP 307 (temporary). app/page.tsx:7 does the same with redirect("/landing") for anything that reaches it. So the root URL, the one that gets typed, linked and shared, never returns a 200. Meanwhile app/landing/page.tsx:29 sets canonical /landing and lib/seo/routes.ts:26 puts /landing in the sitemap at priority 1.0, so /landing is the declared homepage. Pulling the other way, app/layout.tsx:59 declares `alternates: { canonical: "/" }` as the site-wide fallback, with the comment "Pages without their own canonical fall back to the site root rather than competing with each other": that fallback names a URL that always redirects. It is latent today because all 71 pages set their own canonical (see seo-22), so nothing currently inherits it, but the next page added without a pageMetadata call will canonicalise to a redirect.
impact: Branded results show vulnradar.dev/landing rather than vulnradar.dev, which reads as less authoritative for the site's own name. A temporary redirect also tells Google the arrangement may change, so it keeps evaluating both URLs instead of consolidating cleanly, and every cold homepage visit pays an extra round trip before the first byte of content. Small in absolute terms, but it applies to the single highest-authority URL on the domain.
recommendation: Serve the landing content at / instead of redirecting to it. In middleware.ts:284-289, replace NextResponse.redirect with NextResponse.rewrite(new URL(ROUTES.LANDING, request.url)) for the anonymous root case, so / returns 200 with the landing HTML; the signed-in branch keeps redirecting to /dashboard. Then set the landing canonical to "/" in app/landing/page.tsx:29 and change the sitemap entry at lib/seo/routes.ts:26 from "/landing" to "/", and 301 /landing to / so the old URL consolidates. If the redirect is kept instead, at minimum change it to a 308 (`NextResponse.redirect(url, 308)`) so it is declared permanent, and change the root layout fallback at app/layout.tsx:59 to "/landing" so it names a URL that actually renders.

title: Adding or removing a scan tag no-ops on failure in both the history and dashboard copies: no error, no revert, no indication the click was received
description: app/history/page.tsx:305-319 (`handleAddTag`) and :321-331 (`handleRemoveTag`) POST to API.SCAN_TAGS and do all their work inside `if (res.ok)`. There is no else, no catch at all (an unhandled rejection on a dropped connection), and no error state. app/dashboard/page.tsx:389-400 and :402-412 are the same two functions copied verbatim with the same omission. The tag input at components/history/scan-tags.tsx clears on submit regardless, so the typed tag disappears and never appears in the list. Removing a tag on a failed request leaves the chip in place with no explanation. These are the two handlers AUDIT-011#form-01 did not cover on this page (it named handleSaveNotes at :389 in the pre-refactor numbering).
impact: Tagging is how a user organises scan history, and the failure is completely invisible: the input clears exactly as it does on success, so the user believes the tag was applied and only discovers otherwise when they filter by it later and get nothing. The missing catch also means a network drop produces an unhandled promise rejection rather than any handled path.
recommendation: Wrap all four handlers in try/catch and surface a failure. The history page already has a rendered error slot pattern in its clear-history dialog (`clearError` at :667-669); add an equivalent transient line under the tag row, or reuse the toast used elsewhere on the page. At minimum, do not clear the input in components/history/scan-tags.tsx until the parent's promise resolves, so a failed add leaves the user's text where they can retry it.

title: /repos auto-dismisses its only error banner after 8 seconds while the empty list it explains stays on screen
description: app/repos/page.tsx:142-147 runs `const t = setTimeout(() => setError(null), 8000)` whenever `error` becomes non-null. The error strings it clears are load failures, not transient confirmations: `loadWorkingSet` sets "Failed to load repositories." at :172 and :181 and sets `setRepos([])` alongside it, and the init effect sets "Failed to load your GitHub connection status." at :200. Eight seconds later the banner disappears while the repo list it was explaining is still empty, and nothing in the page then accounts for the emptiness. Separately, `loadSummaries` at :150-160 returns early on `!res.ok` with no error at all, so the per-repo "last scanned" column silently reads as never-scanned.
impact: A user who was reading something else when the page loaded, or who tabs back a few seconds later, sees an empty repository list with no error and no explanation, which reads as "you have no repos selected" rather than "the fetch failed". Auto-dismissal is right for a success toast and wrong for a failure whose cause is still true, and this page has only the one error surface.
recommendation: In app/repos/page.tsx:142-147, keep the auto-dismiss only for transient action errors and make load failures sticky, with a Retry button next to the message that recalls the failed loader. The list's own empty branch should also distinguish "no repos in your working set" from "we could not load them", the way components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:248-255 already does for its own list (once state-04 is fixed).

title: The host risk-score trend chart renders identically for still-loading, fetch-failed and not-applicable, so a broken endpoint is indistinguishable from a chart that has nothing to draw
description: components/host/danger-score-trend.tsx:43-59 fetches the trend endpoint, returns early on `!res.ok` at :48 without touching state, and catches at :51-53 with a comment only. `points` therefore stays null in three different situations, and :63's `if (!points) return null` renders nothing for all of them: the request is still in flight, the request failed, or the response was not ok. The file's own docblock at :32-38 documents the design intent and even records that the sub-case of a known host with fewer than two scans was pulled out of this silence precisely because "silence there read as the chart being broken" (:66-82). The same reasoning applies to the failure case, which was left in the silent bucket. The chart also does not reserve its height, so on a slow response it pops in and shifts the panels below it.
impact: On /host/<hostname>, a persistent failure of GET /api/v3/host/<hostname>/trend removes a documented feature with no trace: the user sees the report without the trend and has no reason to think anything is missing. Combined with AUDIT-012#fe-05 (the request cannot start until the host report resolves), a slow trend also produces a late layout shift under content the user is already reading.
recommendation: Split the null: keep `points === null` for in-flight and render a fixed-height skeleton matching the chart's `h-36 sm:h-40` so the layout does not shift, and add a `failed` state set at :48 and :51 that renders one muted line under the existing heading, "Couldn't load the score history.", rather than removing the section. That matches the treatment the same file already gives the fewer-than-two-scans case at :67-82.

title: app/actions/stripe.ts, the 220-statement checkout and credit-purchase server-action surface, is at 56.36% statements and 53.79% branches
description: Measured: app/actions/stripe.ts is 56.36% statements, 53.79% branches, 53.33% functions over 220 statements, the largest under-60% file in the billing area. It imports from lib/billing/browserbase-usage (line 21) and is the entry point users hit to start a checkout and to buy AI, GitHub-review, and Browserbase credit packs. The lower-level catalogs and usage modules around it are all at or near 100% (catalog.ts 100%, ai-credit-catalog.ts 100%, browserbase-credit-catalog.ts 100%, github-credit-catalog.ts 100%, stripe-catalog.ts 100%, plan-limits.ts 100%), so as with the updater in cov-06 the pattern is well-tested primitives with an untested orchestrator. Nearly half the branches are the error, already-subscribed, wrong-plan, and mismatched-currency arms that decide what the user is actually charged for.
impact: Roughly half the decision points on the path that creates a Stripe checkout session are unexercised. A regression in a branch that picks the price id or the quantity charges the wrong amount, and the failure is only visible once a customer complains or the operator reconciles Stripe by hand.
recommendation: Add tests/app/actions/stripe.test.ts with the Stripe SDK mocked, asserting one case per branch that selects a price or quantity: each credit pack maps to its catalog price id, a user already on the target plan is rejected rather than double-charged, an unknown pack id is rejected, and a Stripe API error surfaces as a handled error rather than a thrown server action.

title: The docs component library exports a purpose-built ParamTable and DocsStepCard that no docs page renders, while the API reference renders its parameters with inline markup instead
description: components/docs/index.ts wildcard-exports fourteen modules. Two exported components have no consumer: ParamTable at components/docs/docs-table.tsx:91-164 (74 lines including its doc comment) and DocsStepCard at components/docs/docs-steps.tsx:47-79 (33 lines including its props interface). Neither identifier occurs anywhere in the repo outside its own declaration. ParamTable is the more pointed case: it takes EndpointParam[] (components/docs/docs-types.ts:24) and renders the Parameter/Type/Required/Default/Description table with a conditional Default column, and app/docs/api/page.tsx does supply that exact data, declaring pathParams or queryParams on thirteen endpoint objects (lines 83, 112, 275, 283, 436, 476, 500, 562, 597, 755, 780, 862, 898). Those endpoints are rendered at app/docs/api/page.tsx:1211-1212 by EndpointCard, which at components/docs/docs-endpoint-card.tsx:52-95 renders both param lists with its own hand-written markup rather than calling ParamTable. DocsStepCard is the card variant of DocsSteps (docs-steps.tsx:12), which is used; only the card form is dead. Total 107 lines.
impact: Two rendering paths exist for the same API-reference data and only one is reachable, so a styling or accessibility fix applied to ParamTable never shows up on /docs/api. The docs barrel advertises components that cannot be dropped into any page and expected to match what the site already looks like.
recommendation: Pick one: either delete ParamTable (components/docs/docs-table.tsx:91-164) and DocsStepCard (components/docs/docs-steps.tsx:47-79), 107 lines, or have components/docs/docs-endpoint-card.tsx:52-95 call ParamTable for pathParams and queryParams and delete its inline markup instead.

title: The AI chat widget keeps private copies of the four renderers that components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx was created to own, so the file whose own comment asks to be kept in sync is not the one the live widget uses
description:
components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx exists to be the shared renderer. Its header at :10-18 says so: "The exact react-markdown component overrides the live chat widget (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx) uses. Kept here ... so any renderer of a stored AI message produces identical output to the widget ... If chat-widget.tsx's copy of these ever changes, this is the one to keep in sync with it (or, better, the one it should import from)." MessageContent's own doc at :123-131 goes further: "This is the single rendering path meant to be shared by the live chat widget and the admin AI-chat viewer, so the two can never drift into two different-looking renderers."

chat-widget.tsx does not import any of it. It defines its own `mdComponents` at :202-283 (byte-identical to messageMarkdownComponents at message-content.tsx:19-96), its own `MarkdownContent` at :283-289, its own `ThinkBlock` at :317-329 (byte-identical to message-content.tsx:111-123), and its own segment renderer at :431-470 that calls parseSegments exactly as MessageContent does at :141-159. Both files independently `import ReactMarkdown from "react-markdown"` and `remarkGfm` (chat-widget.tsx:24-25, message-content.tsx:4-5).

The only consumer of message-content.tsx is app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:9. So the module that documents itself as the shared path is used by one admin page, and the widget it was extracted from still runs the copy.
impact: The bodies are identical today, so nothing is currently wrong on screen. The cost is that the module's stated guarantee is false: a styling or safety change to the chat renderer (a link rel, a code-block escape, the think-tag parser) lands on one of the two and the admin viewer and the live widget diverge, which is precisely what the comment says cannot happen. It is also roughly 130 duplicated lines and a duplicated react-markdown + remark-gfm import graph in the widget that AUDIT-012#fe-02 already flags as 144 KB raw on every page.
recommendation: Delete mdComponents, MarkdownContent and ThinkBlock from components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:202-329 and import messageMarkdownComponents, MarkdownContent and ThinkBlock from @/components/ai-chat/message-content. The widget's :431-470 renderer differs from MessageContent only in that it renders `displayContent` (the typewriter buffer) rather than `content`, so give MessageContent an optional `content` override and use it there too, then delete the fourth copy.

title: PUBLIC_PATHS prefix matching silently exempts session-authenticated mutating endpoints from the middleware CSRF check
description: middleware.ts:273-292 returns early for any path matching PUBLIC_PATHS, before the CSRF block at :316. isExemptFromCsrf (:350-368) is documented as "intentionally narrow ... every entry needs a clear non-CSRF trust boundary" and lists six exact paths, but PUBLIC_PATHS creates a second, prefix-matched exemption list that the comment does not account for. Two session-authenticated mutating endpoints land in it: "/api/v3/badge" (public-paths.ts:154) prefix-matches app/api/v3/badge/site/route.ts's POST (:14), PATCH (:64) and DELETE (:95), all of which require getSession() and write host_badges rows; and API_V3.AUTH.ACCEPT_TOS (public-paths.ts:25) covers app/api/v3/auth/accept-tos/route.ts's POST, which does `UPDATE users SET tos_accepted_at = NOW()` for the session user. Two state-changing GETs are also exempt: app/api/v3/stripe/setup-products/route.ts and setup-webhook/route.ts (public-paths.ts:130-131) create live Stripe products/prices and a live Stripe webhook endpoint, and a GET is carried by a SameSite=Lax cookie on a top-level navigation, so a link an admin clicks is enough to fire them.
impact: The CSRF middleware is the app's stated defence for mutating API calls, and these routes silently sit outside it. SameSite=Lax on the session cookie still blocks the cross-site POST cases in current browsers, so this is defence-in-depth rather than a live exploit - but the GET-triggered Stripe setup routes are reachable by a plain link click from an attacker page, and any future same-site-but-different-origin position (a subdomain takeover) collapses the Lax protection for the badge and accept-tos writes too.
recommendation: In middleware.ts, move the `if (pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/") && !isExemptFromCsrf(pathname))` CSRF block above the `if (isPublicPath)` early return at :273 so being publicly reachable no longer implies being CSRF-exempt, and add the genuinely unauthenticated POST endpoints (login, signup, forgot-password, reset-password, 2fa/verify, contact, demo-scan, unsubscribe) to isExemptFromCsrf only if they actually need it - they are same-origin form posts, so most will pass the check unchanged. Separately, convert app/api/v3/stripe/setup-products and setup-webhook from GET to POST since both mutate external state.

title: The crawl page picker is the best-built selection UI in the product and should be kept as is
description: components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx (283 lines), rendered from app/dashboard/page.tsx:963-970. Persistent footer toolbar with 'N of M selected (max L)', a search filter, and Select all / Clear all. Pre-selects up to the plan cap at :55-64; over-cap rows are disabled at 40% opacity with an explanatory banner. useModalA11y provides focus trap, Escape and focus restore. Mobile works at 320px via max-h-[80vh] with a min-h-0 flex-1 scroll list and text-base sm:text-xs to stop iOS zoom. The backend is a real bulk endpoint: one request carries the whole array and app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:235-272 re-validates and re-enforces the plan cap server-side.
impact: None. Recorded so it is not swept up in a bulk-action removal pass: deleting it does not remove clutter, it removes the crawl feature or forces every crawl to scan every discovered page at the user's expense.
recommendation: Keep. Two optional nits: the rows are buttons with aria-pressed and a fake check glyph rather than real checkboxes, so assistive tech does not announce them as checkboxes; and defaulting to everything pre-selected means a user who wants three pages must deselect the rest.

title: Inter and JetBrains Mono are imported and never applied; the site ships in system-ui
description: app/layout.tsx:39-43 imports Inter and JetBrains_Mono from next/font/google but assigns both to underscore-prefixed unused consts, and their --font-inter and --font-jetbrains-mono variables are never applied. app/layout.tsx:170 is <body className="font-sans antialiased"> and tailwind.config.mjs has no fontFamily extension, so the real stack is Tailwind v4's ui-sans-serif / ui-monospace defaults.
impact: Either two font downloads are being paid for and discarded, or the intended typography was never shipped. Both are worth knowing before any design work.
recommendation: Decide which was intended: wire the CSS variables into tailwind.config.mjs, or remove the imports. Note the system stack is what every existing surface was visually tuned against, so switching to Inter is a visual change, not a no-op.

title: components/ui/badge.tsx is the one primitive that hardcodes Tailwind palette colours and ignores dark mode
description: components/ui/badge.tsx:16-19 defines info as bg-blue-500/10 text-blue-600, success as bg-green-500/10 text-green-600, warning as bg-amber-500/10 text-amber-600 and error as bg-red-500/10 text-red-600. These bypass the token set and do not respond to dark mode. The codebase is otherwise clean: zero bg-gray-*, text-gray-*, bg-slate-*, bg-zinc-* or border-gray-* anywhere in app/ or components/. Related: app/globals.css:9 safelists literal palette colours for role badges, :487-575 hardcodes hover and selection surfaces as literal hsl() with !important, --surface-1/2/3 are defined at :210-213 and used nowhere, and --sidebar-* is wired into tailwind.config.mjs:64-73 but never defined in CSS so those utilities resolve to nothing. Separately components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:114 uses text-emerald-500 where every other success indicator uses text-[hsl(var(--success))].
impact: Four badge variants render the same colour in both themes, and the variant names (info/success/warning/error) form a second severity vocabulary competing with the real one.
recommendation: Move the four variants onto --success, --warning and --destructive tokens. Fix badge-preview.tsx:114. Remove the dead --surface-* and --sidebar-* declarations.

title: isNavItemActive has two identical ternary branches, so NavItem.exact does nothing
description: components/docs/docs-nav.ts:152-154 is `return item.exact ? pathname === item.href : pathname === item.href;`. NavItem.exact is declared at components/docs/docs-types.ts:12 and set on /docs at docs-nav.ts:21. Used by docs-sidebar.tsx:48 and docs-mobile-nav.tsx:94.
impact: Correct today only because every nav href is a distinct page. A future prefix-matched entry will silently fail to highlight.
recommendation: Either implement the non-exact branch as `pathname === item.href || pathname.startsWith(`${item.href}/`)`, or delete the helper and inline the equality.

title: Seven touch targets under 44px in the docs and legal navigation, worst at 20px
description: components/legal/legal-toc.tsx:26-28 has no vertical padding at all, giving about 20px, and it is the primary navigation for 15-clause legal documents. Others: app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:433 about 26px; components/docs/docs-code-block.tsx:53-60 about 27px; components/legal/legal-nav.tsx:45 about 30px; components/docs/docs-toc.tsx:73-78 about 32px and this is the mobile TOC (xl:hidden); components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:39 about 36px; components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:81 about 36px.
impact: Legal and docs navigation is hard to operate accurately on a phone.

title: The changelog has no pagination fallback, so without IntersectionObserver it is a permanent loading state
